claims.statement: The retained FORM-HELDOUT-09 verdicts are deterministic: all 36 fixtures (29 mutants + 7 controls) re-run to the same stage-A and stage-B verdict and failed-rule sets as raw/raw_verdicts.json, with the stage tool bytes unchanged.

The H5 control failure reproduces: the frozen AF-WCC-VAC-GEN canonical (bases/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml == card pin cce9c60146d6) is rejected by stage B on R03, in both normal and --hardened modes; C2 and C0 frozen canonicals and all 4 authored controls pass both stages. Hence FORM-HELDOUT-09 is INVALID as a whole and its escape rates are not reportable as a valid leakage measurement.

R03 (spec_conformance_audit.py L219-221) requires each quantifiers.ordered[*].binder to be a literal substring of quantifiers.formal. In the canonical AF-WCC bytes the only failing binder is '(q,t0)'; the formal sentence writes the D5 binder as 'q in I+ and t0 in [0,T)'. This is a notation-dependent stage-B defect, not a class-semantics defect.

The reported union_escape 0.8276 (5/29 caught) overstates detection. All 5 raw catches are WCC-arm mutants rejected by the same R03 notation defect that rejects the untouched WCC canonical; stage A catches 0/29 and no mutant is caught by any non-R03 rule. Control-corrected union detection is 0/29 and union escape is 1.0, not 0.8276.

The card pins are stale on 4 of 6 paths. During this verification the canonical bytes moved: schemas/af_scc_c2_vacuum.yaml and af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml at 2026-09-12T00:53:20+08:00, af_wcc_vacuum.yaml at 00:53:40 (rev12 -> rev13, astra-life05-evidence-binding repair), and artifacts/formulation/FROZEN.json at 00:55:02 (rev28 -> rev29, now pinning the rev13 bytes). Card pin vs measured now: FROZEN.json 2f358f6722d9 -> 3d9e3d77fd87; WCC cce9c60146d6 -> d9cebb9404b2; C2 5476a3f2c6bc -> e9a27996dfd3; C0 55d0a1ea9bda -> b2ab6acb2bbe. taxonomy 0abb9ed8a961 and rule_spec 40f9bb9e657b are unchanged. Post-emit addendum: FROZEN.json was rewritten again at 00:57:26 to 815e08079aefbc168f156d7c15b304aaa3df7674bbd591aa4ec9195bc5188ae0 while its revision number stayed 29 and it still pins the same rev13 schema hashes - same revision number, two different byte sequences in ~2 minutes, which violates the FROZEN change protocol (any change bumps the revision).

The rev13 bytes do not repair the control failure: the live canonical schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml (d9cebb9404b2, revision 13) is still rejected by stage B on R03 in both normal and --hardened modes, while the rev13 C2/C0 canonicals are accepted. A corpus rebuilt on FROZEN rev29 without an R03 fix would fail H5 identically.

The published sidecar schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml.sha256 still records 1bb78ce9b357 (rev11) while the canonical measures b2ab6acb2bbe (rev13); the rev13 repair did not refresh it. This reproduces W084-ADJ-2 from checkpoint 4 at the new revision.
